subject: Urgent: 503s and latency on reserved throughput for LedgerPay — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Tim Foster <tim.foster@ledgerpay.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s + latency spike affecting reserved throughput (URGENT)

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and per-request latency for our reserved endpoints around 07:10 PDT this morning. The symptoms: 12–17% 503 rate on our production routes, p95 latency up from 220ms to ~1.2s, and a steady token-generation throughput drop despite our reserved capacity being listed as healthy in the console. Our traffic profile hasn’t changed on LedgerPay’s side — same request mix as yesterday.

Attached is a log bundle (ledgerpay_error_snapshot_0315.zip) with request/response traces and the customer-facing error IDs (ERR-LP-3xx). We’re also seeing queue depth rising on our side. This is putting live payment flows at risk; we’ve seen a handful of timeouts on settlement requests.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood’s side of the reserved pool and whether you can remediate quickly? We need a bridge and ETA — this is high business impact for us.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Foster
SRE Lead, LedgerPay

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s + latency spike affecting reserved throughput (URGENT)

Sharing preliminary technical readout from the on-call investigation (engineers already on a bridge):

Observations (07:05–10:50 PDT):
- Cluster-level inbound load unchanged; however, one dedicated GPU pool (pool-us-west-3b-dcap-42) is showing sustained high GPU utilization and memory pressure across shards.
- KV cache churn is higher than usual for LedgerPay’s model variant (cache hit rate dropped ~18%), which increases per-request compute.
- Worker queue depth increased; autoscaler did not trigger additional nodes because pool-specific capacity policy prevented burst allocation for reserved pools.
- Error profile: most 5xx are internal 503s from the pool proxy layer (proxy timeouts when worker backpressure occurs).

Immediate mitigations enacted (11:05–11:18):
- Temporarily reclassified a small set of non-production pools as preemptible and reclaimed two GPUs to give headroom to the reserved pool (reduced 503 rate from ~15% to ~6%).
- Applied a short-term routing rule to steer low-priority batch traffic away from LedgerPay’s pool.

Next actions (need approval to proceed):
1) Emergency capacity boost: allocate 6 additional GPUs to pool-us-west-3b-dcap-42 for 48 hours (estimated incremental infra cost: $9k for 48h).
2) Moderate reconfiguration: enable controlled burst in autoscaler for reserved pools while we triage root cause.
3) Longer-term: tune KV cache eviction thresholds for this model variant and run a load test against the new config.

I’ve attached a small diagnostic dump. More metrics and traces are in SUP-19872. If execs approve (Lauren / Aditya), we can spin the extra capacity in ~30 minutes.

Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Executive summary & ask — LedgerPay reserved throughput shortfall (decision required)

Team / Aditya / Priyom —

Summary: LedgerPay experienced a reserved-pool throughput shortfall on 2028-03-15 that degraded service (503s and elevated p95). Engineering confirmed the immediate driver is pool-level GPU saturation compounded by KV cache churn and a restrictive burst policy that prevented autoscaler relief. Our short-term mitigations reduced the 5xx rate but did not fully restore contract SLA.

Ask (decision requested):
- Approve emergency capacity boost: +6 GPUs to pool-us-west-3b-dcap-42 for 48 hours (approx. $9k infra). This buys time to tune eviction thresholds and re-run the workload test.
- Approve temporary customer concession: one weekly service credit and a one-time account credit of $7,500 to LedgerPay to acknowledge interruption risk to pilot. This is to be used if we cannot restore SLA to contractual levels in the next 48 hours.

Business impact: high — pilot at risk, expansion timeline stalls until stability is proven. Marissa, please coordinate customer comms if we move forward with the boost + credit.

If approved I’ll instruct SRE to initiate capacity spin-up immediately and let LedgerPay know the bridge outcome.

Lauren Bishop
